[|AI|]: Yes, clubs in the Isthmian League have restrictions on how much they can spend on players' salaries, in order to promote financial stability and prevent excessive spending. The precise limits vary depending on the individual league and each club's financial situation, but generally, clubs are expected to adhere to strict wage budgets.

To ensure that they don't overspend on player wages, clubs in the Isthmian League must carefully manage their finances and prioritize spending in areas that will provide the most value for the club. This may involve setting clear wage caps for individual players or agreeing on collective agreements with player representatives to ensure that the club can afford to pay its players' wages.

Clubs may also use performance-based contracts as a way of controlling wage costs, whereby player salaries are linked to on-field performance and results. This provides an incentive for players to perform well, while also ensuring that the club only pays for quality players who are contributing to the team.

Additionally, many clubs in the Isthmian League rely on volunteer support or part-time staff to keep costs down. This can range from unpaid management staff to players who receive expenses rather than salaries, and it enables the club to stretch its budget further.

Overall, while operating under financial constraints can be challenging for clubs in the Isthmian League, it promotes financial stability and ensures that clubs only spend what they can afford, leading to a more sustainable model in the long term.
